fields.label: Groundwater Zone Soil Thickness
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the groundwater layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 3 is from Table 3 - Thickness of the aquifer layer from McKone et al. 2001 (Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information.

fields.label: Density of Solid Material in Aquifer
fields.help: Enter the density of soil solids in the groundwater layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 2,600 is the value used by the CalTOX model (see Table 1 of: CalEPA (California Environmental Protection Agency), Department of Toxic Substances Control. 1996. The Distribution of California Landscape Variables for CalTOX. Draft (February).

fields.label: Fraction Sand
fields.help: Enter the fraction of the soil layer that is sand. Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.25 is professional judgment. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: Organic Carbon Fraction
fields.help: Enter the mass fraction of the soil solids which is made up of organic carbon in the soil layer. Valid values are > 0. The default value of 0.008 is the U.S. average in Table 16 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: pH
fields.help: Enter the pH of the soil layer. Valid values are 0 to 14. The default value of 6.8 is professional judgment. Typical sources of site-specific values include the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Web Soil Survey (Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Web Soil Survey. Available online at https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/.).

fields.label: Porosity
fields.help: Enter the volume fraction of pore space in the groundwater layer. Valid values are 0 to 1. The default value of 0.2 is the value used for the sediment zone for California residential sites by version 1.5 of the CalTOX model (see Table VI of: CalEPA (California Environmental Protection Agency), Department of Toxic Substances Control. 1993. Parameter Values and Ranges for CalTOX. Draft (July).

fields.label: Hg Methylation Rate
fields.help: Enter the methylation rate for divalent mercury (Hg) in the groundwater layer. Valid values are ≥ 0. The default value of 0.001 is the maximum potential rate in flooded soils (humus and peat) under anaerobic conditions from Porvari and Verta 1995 (Methylmercury Production in Flooded Soils: a Laboratory Study), as reported on page B-21 of U.S. EPA 1997 (Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information.

fields.label: Hg Reduction Rate
fields.help: Enter the reduction rate for divalent mercury in the groundwater layer. Valid values are ≥ 0. The default value of 3.25E-06 is the value for soils at a depth of 20 cm and a water content of 10%, calculated based on information from Lindberg 1996 (Forests and the Global Biogeochemical Cycle of Mercury: The Importance of Understanding Air/Vegetation Exchange Processes), and Carpi and Lindberg 1997 (Sunlight-Mediated Emission of Elemental Mercury from Soil Amended with Municipal Sewage Sludge), as reported on page B-20 of U.S. EPA 1997 (Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information.

fields.label: Hg Oxidation Rate
fields.help: Enter the oxidation rate for elemental mercury in the groundwater layer. Valid values are ≥ 0. The default value of 1E-08 is a small, non-zero value, whereas soil oxidation is shown as 0 in Table B-2 of U.S. EPA 1997 (Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information.

fields.label: Hg Demethylation Rate
fields.help: Enter the demethylation rate for methyl mercury in the groundwater layer. Valid values are ≥ 0. The default value of 0.06 is the maximum potential rate in flooded soils (humus) under anaerobic conditions from Porvari and Verta 1995 (Methylmercury Production in Flooded Soils: a Laboratory Study), as reported on page B-22 of U.S. EPA 1997 (Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment). See the TRIM User Guide Appendix for full reference information.
